rationale: The student added 30+20=50 and 7+6=13, writing 513 side-by-side instead of regrouping 10 ones into 1 ten. Demonstrating 'make-a-ten' shows how a sum of ones greater than 9 bundles into a ten and remaining ones.

script.focus: ten ones regrouping into one ten

intent: Demonstrate make-a-ten on the place-value with values [15]. Tutor points at: ten ones regrouping into one ten

frames.caption: Here are 15 ones. That is too many for the ones place: it can only hold 0 to 9.
Bundle ten of them. Ten ones make one ten, so the bundle moves to the tens place. 5 ones are left.
Write 1 in the tens place and 5 in the ones place: 15. One digit per place.

judgement.reasoning: The student wrote 513 for 37 + 26 because they do not realize the ones place cannot hold two digits and that 13 ones must be regrouped into 1 ten and 3 ones. This demo directly addresses that rule ('the ones place can only hold 0 to 9') by showing 15 ones bundled into 1 ten and 5 ones, clearly highlighting place-value constraints. It is simpler than full 2-digit addition and does not leak the answer to 37 + 26.
judgement.verdict: A teacher would definitely use this concise demo to explain why two digits cannot sit in the ones place before returning to the full addition problem.
